slides.text:
Positional arguments are the words after the command that are not flags. Cobra hands them to `Run` as a slice of strings, and can check them before `Run` starts.

The sketch is not Go.
slides.code:
$ app resize photo.png 800
command: resize
args:    [photo.png 800]

slides.text:
Three sessions:

- **Session 1:** reading `args`
- **Session 2:** the ready-made checks in `Args`
- **Session 3:** your own checks, flags beside arguments and corner cases

Cobra fills `args` with the words typed after the command, flags removed. It is an ordinary `[]string`, so you read it with an index, `len` and `range`.

The user may type any number of words, or none.

slides.text:
A command can check its arguments before `Run` starts, with its `Args` field. When the check fails, cobra prints the error with the usage and `Run` does not start.

The snippet is pseudo code.
slides.code:
Args: <check the words>
Run:  <starts only if the check passes>

slides.text:
Cobra ships ready-made checks, all under `cobra`:

- `NoArgs`: no words
- `ExactArgs(n)`: exactly n
- `MinimumNArgs(n)`: at least n
- `MaximumNArgs(n)`: at most n
- `RangeArgs(min, max)`: between min and max

exercises.title: Exactly two arguments
exercises.guide: Copy needs a source and a destination, nothing more or less.

chunks.guide: A command that reads two arguments.

notes.text: Rejects the call unless exactly 2 words come

exercises.title: One argument too few
exercises.guide: The user runs `rename a.txt`. What happens?
options: Run starts and panics at args[1]
Cobra prompts for the missing argument
Cobra shows the usage and still starts Run
Cobra reports the count and Run never starts
exercises.explanation: `ExactArgs(2)` runs before `Run`. With one word it returns an error, cobra prints it with the usage, and `Run` never starts, so `args[1]` is never read.

exercises.title: One or more arguments
exercises.guide: Remove every file the user names, and refuse an empty call.

notes.text: Accepts one word or more, rejects none

exercises.title: Require at least one
exercises.guide: The command needs one or more names. Loop over all of them.

exercises.title: Between one and two
exercises.guide: Back up a folder to an optional destination.

chunks.guide: The destination is optional, so it needs a default.
Allow one or two words, no fewer and no more.

notes.text: Both limits are included: 1 or 2 words pass

exercises.title: What is Args for here?
exercises.guide: Read the code, then pick what `Args` does.
options: Rejects any word typed after the command
Hides the command from the help output
Stops the command from reading flags
Makes the command read its words from stdin
exercises.explanation: `NoArgs` fails the check when any word comes after `version`, so a typo like `app version now` is an error instead of being ignored.

slides.text:
When the ready-made checks are not enough, write your own: a function that looks at the words and returns an error to reject them, or nil to accept. Checks can also be combined.

The snippet is pseudo code.
slides.code:
check(command, words):
    if the words are wrong:
        return an error
    return nothing

slides.text: Before your check runs, cobra takes the flags out of the command line. Only the words left reach `args`.

chunks.guide: An `Args` check is a function that returns an error to reject the words, or nil to accept them.

notes.text: Cobra calls this before Run, an error stops the command
Fails when the word is not a whole number

chunks.guide: Give the function to `Args`, by name.

notes.text: No parentheses: cobra calls the function itself

exercises.title: Flags beside arguments
exercises.guide: Greet a name as many times as a flag says.

chunks.guide: The name is an argument. How many times is a flag.
Register the flag. `ExactArgs(1)` counts only the name, never the flag.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: The user runs `app --name bob alice carol`.
exercises.explanation: The flag takes the next word as its value, so `bob` is `name`. Only `alice` and `carol` are left in `args`.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.explanation: A bare `--` ends the flags. Everything after it is an argument, even a word that looks like a flag.

exercises.guide: Deploy only to an environment from a fixed list.

chunks.guide: List the words allowed, then require exactly one that is on the list.

notes.text: Passes only when every check inside passes
Rejects any word that is not in ValidArgs

exercises.title: Limit the words
exercises.guide: Accept exactly one word, and only a word from the list.

exercises.title: What does it print?
exercises.guide: The user runs `app serve fast now`.
exercises.explanation: Without an `Args` field, a command with no subcommands accepts any words. Both reach `args`, so it prints 2.

exercises.title: Any words on a root
exercises.guide: Echo any words, on a root that also has a subcommand.

chunks.guide: A root with subcommands rejects unknown words as an unknown command. `ArbitraryArgs` lets them through to `Run`.

notes.text: Accepts any number of words, even none
